title: Anatomical homeostasis may exist mainly to correct mutation-induced deviations

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Anatomical homeostasis may exist mainly to correct mutation-induced deviations

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The primary reason for anatomical homeostasis in regulative development and regeneration may be to correct deviations from target morphology caused by mutations, rather than to repair damage.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Evolutionary Aspects › Multi-Scale Autonomy Potentiates the Speed of Evolution

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The primary reason for the anatomical homeostasis seen in regulative development and regeneration may be for dealing, not with damage, but with deviations from target morphology induced by mutations.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Evolutionary Aspects › Multi-Scale Autonomy Potentiates the Speed of Evolution”. Scope: Evolution of regulative development and regeneration in animals

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-30: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.43

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Existing comparative and perturbation data can test whether homeostasis buffers both mutation and damage in selected systems. They have little power to assign a single primary historical selective cause.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across taxa, compare the evolution and strength of regulative development with historical mutation load and injury exposure, and test whether correction mechanisms preferentially buffer genetic versus injury-induced deviations.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Cross-taxon measures of anatomical homeostasis are sparse.

Primary evolutionary reason is difficult to infer from extant data.

Mutation and damage correction often use the same mechanisms.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.4
analysis feasibility: 0.48
discriminating power: 0.3
data adequacy: 0.3
data existence: 0.62

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Anatomical homeostasis can be shown to reduce error after cuts and after experimental displacements, and both results fit a system shaped by injury, by mutation, or by both. The claim is about the primary evolutionary reason. Present physiological and phylogenetic records do not separate that historical purpose from the other.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Repair of injury and correction of a mutational displacement use the same homeostasis measurements, so either selective history remains compatible with the same present-day data.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: A mechanism that corrects both wounds and mutational deviations does not record which of those roles was the primary historical reason.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.1
operationalizability: 0.2
analysis feasibility: 0.15
discriminating power: 0.15
data existence: 0.15
